subject: Business Models
title: Non-Compete Clauses
description: A fast breakdown of Non-Compete Clauses for builders.

hook.text: Quit your franchise agreement, and you can't open any similar business within 25 miles for 2 years.

buildup.text: Non-compete clauses prevent former franchisees from using knowledge and skills to compete against the brand.

discovery.text: A former Subway owner can't open a sandwich shop. Their industry expertise becomes legally useless.

twist.text: Some franchises apply non-competes to low-wage workers. Jimmy John's had sandwich makers sign them until sued.

climax.text: Non-competes protect brands but trap people. The FTC is moving to ban most non-compete agreements.

punchline.text: Learn the business, leave, can't use what you learned. That's the clause.

quiz.question: What did Jimmy John's controversially require of its workers?

details.summary: Non-compete clauses in franchise agreements restrict franchisees from operating competing businesses during and often for 1 to 2 years after the franchise relationship ends. These clauses protect the franchisor's trade secrets and system but limit franchisee career freedom and exit options.
details.whyItMatters: Non-compete clauses affect what franchisees can do if the franchise fails or the relationship sours. Overly broad non-competes can trap franchisees in unprofitable situations by preventing them from using their industry expertise elsewhere after.
takeaways: Post-term non-competes typically restrict competing businesses for 1 to 2 years
Geographic scope and industry definition determine how restrictive the clause actually is
Overly broad non-competes can trap franchisees by limiting career options after exit

faq.question: What makes a franchise non-compete clause enforceable?
faq.answer: Courts evaluate reasonableness based on geographic scope, duration, and industry restriction breadth. A 1-year non-compete within 10 miles for the same cuisine type is more likely enforceable than a 5-year nationwide ban on all food service. State laws vary significantly on enforcement standards.

faq.question: Can franchisees negotiate non-compete terms?
faq.answer: Rarely in standard franchise agreements, which are typically non-negotiable. Experienced multi-unit operators and master franchisees have more leverage to negotiate narrower terms. Franchisees should have a franchise attorney review non-compete scope before signing.
